intelligence.simple_view: Today we learned thirty-two things, and we squeezed them down into four big lessons — like squeezing a whole bag of oranges into one glass of juice. The calendar is the biggest job: the whole page IS the calendar, and you tap a day to see everything about that day. The colors are deep and pretty, never neon. And everything we build has to be proven — not just said, but shown working — before we call it done.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — thirty-two notes came in today, dear, and we boiled them down to four lessons, the way you boil a big pot of stock down to the good rich part. The calendar is the day's work, love — the whole page is the calendar, and you tap a day to see its world. The colors are deep and elegant, dear, never loud. And nothing is called done until you can see it working with your own eyes, love — that is the rule that holds the whole house together.
intelligence.naya_view: I distill ten into one, every day, and I never skip a day. When the machine refuses, I finish by hand and say so plainly — which group failed, what the error was, which groups were machine-filed, which were hand-distilled. I never claim a note is live on the Hub until it is on the page.
